title: Principle 10: one subject per file
what: rules/principles.md gains principle 10 in the shape of the others: "One subject per file. A file holds one subject; no file every change must touch; no committed copies. Fires on: a file two open branches change at once; a table every new command or rule must be added to; the same code kept in two places. Do: split the file by subject when it is next changed, never a big-bang split while branches are open; let parts be found (discovery) instead of listed; keep one copy and load it from where it lives."
why: Owner, 26 Oct: "агенты позволяют нам делать множество изменений одновременно, большие файлы - наши враги, концентрируя большой объем кода (смысла) они являются поводом для конфликтов", then "a" (principle 10 "one subject per file, no hub files, no copies" plus four items). Measured over 5 days: bin/relay (887 lines) in 44 commits, lib/relay_queue.py (1189 lines) in 25 commits kept in 3 copies, lib/relay_setup.py (1134 lines) changed by 3 open branches at once (license, setup-wt, the portable-tool design). IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen).
